name: Pregnancy Checklist
description: A trimester-by-trimester guide to prenatal care and preparing for baby.

items.text: Take a prenatal vitamin daily
items.note: Ask your provider which one is right for you.

items.text: Call to schedule your first prenatal appointment

Review your insurance coverage and out-of-pocket costs
Note your last period date and any early symptoms to share
Stop alcohol and smoking, and review medications with your doctor
Choose an obstetrician, family doctor, or midwife
Attend your first prenatal visit and any early screenings
Adjust your diet toward balanced, regular meals as tolerated
Stay hydrated and rest when fatigue hits
Start a simple folder or app to track appointments and notes
Decide who to tell and when you feel ready
Attend your anatomy ultrasound around the midpoint
Ask your provider about recommended prenatal classes
Begin gentle, provider-approved movement or exercise
Start your baby registry and compare big-ticket items
Look into parental leave and notify your workplace
Plan the nursery layout and order furniture with lead times in mind
Attend more frequent prenatal visits as scheduled
Discuss your birth preferences with your provider
Take a childbirth, breastfeeding, or newborn care class
Install and inspect the infant car seat
Learn the signs of labor and when to call your provider

Wash and put away newborn clothes and blankets

Prepare and freeze a few easy meals for the early weeks

faq.q: When should I schedule my first prenatal appointment?
faq.a: Most providers want to see you around 8 weeks, so call as soon as you have a positive test or confirm your pregnancy. Booking early helps establish care and gives you a chance to ask questions. Your provider will then set a schedule for the visits that follow.

faq.q: What should I avoid during pregnancy?
faq.a: Common guidance includes avoiding alcohol, smoking, and certain foods like raw fish and unpasteurized cheese. Check medications and supplements with your provider before taking them. Everyone's situation is different, so ask your doctor or midwife about any specific restrictions that apply to your pregnancy.

faq.q: How often will I have prenatal appointments?
faq.a: Visits are often monthly in early pregnancy, then more frequent in the third trimester, usually every two weeks and then weekly near your due date. Your provider sets the exact schedule based on your health. Keep a list of questions to bring to each appointment so you don't forget.

faq.q: When should I start preparing the nursery?
faq.a: Many parents tackle the nursery in the second trimester, when energy often returns, and finish early in the third. There's no strict rule, so plan around how you feel. Focus on the sleep space and a few essentials first; the rest can come together gradually over the weeks.

faq.q: When do I need to pack a hospital bag?
faq.a: Aim to have your bag packed by around 36 weeks, since labor can begin before your due date. Keep it somewhere easy to grab. Packing early removes last-minute stress, so you can focus on getting to the hospital or birth center calmly when contractions start.
